youtubeTitle: She was confined to her home until a few years ago. Now 400 farmers come to her for advice.
caption:
She was confined to her home until a few years ago. Now 400 farmers come to her for advice.

Shobha Devi, 49, from Tikha village in Muzaffarpur district, Bihar, was a homemaker with little outside her household until she joined a Jeevika self-help group in 2020. She completed a 21-day Agri-Entrepreneur Programme run with the Syngenta Foundation India, took a Rs 2 lakh loan and started vermicomposting in 2021 before building an Agri-Entrepreneur Service Centre focused on mushroom cultivation and organic farm inputs. She now advises a network of roughly 400 farmers - mostly women - on soil health, pest management and balanced fertilizer use, while earning about Rs 15,000 a month herself. From confined to her home to running a 400-farmer advisory network - one 21-day course at a time.
